extracted.intended_audience: graduate students or advanced undergraduates studying commutative algebra (readers of the textbook and its exercise solutions)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted exercises, propositions and commentary from a textbook chapter on Noetherian/Artin rings, primary decomposition, constructible sets, Dedekind domains, discrete valuation rings, and completions. Each rubric entry corresponds to a statement to be proved or a structural criterion referred to in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: BG is finitely generated A-algebra (Exercise 7.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a Noetherian ring, B a finitely generated A-algebra, G a finite group of A-automorphisms of B, and BG the set of all elements of B fixed by every element of G. Show that BG is a finitely generated A-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Use Exercise 5.12 (p.68) and Proposition 7.8 (p.81).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finitely generated ring that is a field is finite (Exercise 7.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a finitely generated ring is a field K, then K is a finite field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: Let A be the prime subring of K (A = Z or F_p). Use Proposition 5.7 and Noether Normalization to rule out A = Z and conclude K is a finite degree extension of F_p.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine variety defined by finitely many equations (Exercise 7.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be an affine algebraic variety given by family of equations f_α(t1,...,tn)=0 (α∈I). Show there exists a finite subset I0⊂I such that X is given by f_α=0 for α∈I0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because k[t1,...,tn] is Noetherian, the ideal generated by all f_α is finitely generated; pick generators to obtain I0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion assertions based on chosen elements (Exercise 7.9 hints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prove certain inclusions of ideals/localizations using appropriate choices of elements x_{s+1},...,x_t and x_1 and choices of maximal ideals m1,...,mr+s; show that selected elements become units in appropriate localizations to obtain desired inclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the fact that choices of x_i guarantee unit status in the appropriate localized rings (e.g., x1/1 is a unit in A_{m_{r+1}}) and then deduce inclusions like a m1 ⊂ (x0_1,...,x_t_1), etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Noetherian rings do not necessarily imply global Noetherian (Exercise 7.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a ring such that each local ring A_p is Noetherian. Is A necessarily Noetherian? (Investigate this question.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercises 2.28 and 3.10ii (cf. references in the book). The exercise is intended to guide the reader to counterexamples or necessary extra hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibers of finite type morphism are Noetherian (Exercise 7.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f: A→B is a ring homomorphism of finite type and f*: Spec(B)→Spec(A) is the associated map, show that the fibers of f* are Noetherian subspaces of Spec(B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let p∈Spec(A) and set k = A_p / p A_p. Reduce to showing k⊗_A B is Noetherian. Since B is a quotient of A[x1,...,xn], k⊗_A B is a quotient of k[x1,...,xn].

rubrics_metrics.name: I(V) equals radical(a) (Exercise 7.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: For k algebraically closed, A = k[t1,...,tn], a⊂A ideal, V the variety defined by a, and I(V) the ideal of polynomials vanishing on V. Show I(V) = r(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the Nullstellensatz; the text refers to a previous paragraph where it was proved (Paragraph 6.2.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of freeness/flatness over Noetherian local rings (Exercise 7.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m and residue field k, and M a finitely generated A-module. The following are equivalent: (i) M is free; (ii) M is flat; (iii) the map m⊗M → A⊗M is injective; (iv) Tor_i^A(k,M) = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sketch: choose xi lifting a k-basis of M/mM, let F free with basis ei mapping to xi; show Ker φ vanishes by tensoring with k and using Nakayama and finite generation of Ker since A is Noetherian.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat = locally free for finitely generated modules (Exercise 7.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian and M a finitely generated A-module. Equivalent statements: (i) M is flat; (ii) M_p is a free A_p-module for all prime ideals p; (iii) M_m is a free A_m-module for all maximal ideals m. In other words, flat = locally free.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use localization arguments and the analogous finite-generation/local-freeness results (exercise references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition for submodules of Noetherian modules (Exercise 7.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a ring and M a Noetherian A-module. Show that every submodule N⊂M has a primary decomposition (imitate proofs given earlier for ideals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: If 0⊂M is irreducible, show 0 is primary; work with chains (0:a)⊂(0:a^2)⊂... which stabilize in Noetherian modules to show nilpotence; mimic proofs of ideal cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Associated primes and composition series (Exercise 7.18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian, p a prime ideal and M a finitely generated A-module. Show equivalence: (i) p is an associated prime of M; (ii) there exists x∈M with Ann(x)=p; (iii) there exists a submodule of M isomorphic to A/p. Deduce existence of a chain 0=M0⊂M1⊂...⊂Mr=M with each Mi/M_{i-1} ≅ A/p_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 7.17 and its generalization to modules (Proposition 80) which equates prime ideals belonging to a submodule with ideals (N:x) for x∈M. Construct chain inductively using these primes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness properties of minimal primary decomposition (Exercise 7.19 / Proposition 81)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two minimal decompositions of a submodule W as intersection of irreducible submodules W = ⋂_{i=1}^n U_i = ⋂_{j=1}^m V_j, then n = m; and if M is Noetherian then, after re-indexing, r(U_i : M) = r(V_i : M) for all i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key lemma (Lemma 82): with U1 irreducible and W = U1∩U2 = ⋂ V_j then W = V_i ∩ U2 for some i; proceed by contradiction and induction. Use maps M→M/U_i and irreducibility of zero.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algebra generated by opens and complements (Exercise 7.20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F be smallest collection of subsets of X containing all opens and closed under finite intersections and complements. (i) E∈F iff E is a finite union of sets of the form U∩C where U open and C closed. (ii) If X irreducible and E∈F, then E is dense in X iff E contains a non-empty open set.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove closure properties for finite unions of U∩C to show they form F. For (ii), note density forces some U∩C dense hence C=X and then U⊂E.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructible sets criterion in Noetherian spaces (Exercise 7.21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X Noetherian and E⊂X. E∈F (the algebra of constructible sets) iff for each irreducible closed X0⊂X either E∩X0 ≠ X0 or else E∩X0 contains a non-empty open subset of X0. (Condition (63) in text.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: consider minimal closed X in which E∩X ∉ F; show X irreducible and derive contradictions by looking at nonempty open subsets of X0. Use Exercise 7.20.

rubrics_metrics.name: Openness criterion in Noetherian spaces (Exercise 7.22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let X be Noetherian and E⊂X. E is open in X iff for each irreducible closed subset X0 in X either E∩X0 = ∅ or E∩X0 contains a non-empty open subset of X0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
If E open, condition is immediate. Conversely, assume not open and consider F = X 
bsp;E; argue using minimal closed X0 for which F∩X0 not closed to derive contradiction, showing E fails condition iff not open.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of constructible sets under finite type maps is constructible (Exercise 7.23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A Noetherian, f: A→B finite type, X=Spec(A), Y=Spec(B). For constructible E⊂Y, f*(E) is constructible in X (Chevalley's theorem for finite type morphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to E=U∩C with U open and C closed; reduce to case E open. Since Y Noetherian, E is quasi-compact and hence finite union of Spec(B_g). Reduce further to show f*(Y) constructible by restricting to irreducible components and to case A,B domains and injective f; use earlier exercises referenced (Chapter 5 Exercise 21).

rubrics_metrics.name: f* open mapping ↔ going-down property (Exercise 7.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: With notation as in Exercise 7.23, f* is an open map if and only if f has the going-down property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If f has going-down: show image E=f*(Y) is open by checking that for irreducible closed X0 meeting E, E∩X0 is dense in X0; apply Exercises 7.20–7.22. The text spells out the final inclusion argument using ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flat finite-type maps give open maps (Exercise 7.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and f: A→B is finite type and flat (so B flat as A-module), then f*: Spec(B)→Spec(A) is an open mapping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Exercise 24 and Chapter 5, Exercise 11; reduction uses going-down property or known results about flat finite-type morphisms. The book's hint is 'fairly complete'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grothendieck group K(A) construction and universal property (Exercise 7.26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define C the free abelian group on isomorphism classes F(A) of finitely generated A-modules, D subgroup generated by relations from short exact sequences; K(A)=C/D. (i) K(A) has universal property: any additive function λ on finitely generated modules factors uniquely through K(A). (ii) K(A) is generated by γ(A/p) for prime ideals p. (iii) If A is a field or PID then K(A) ≅ Z. (iv) For finite ring hom f: A→B, restriction of scalars gives f!: K(B)→K(A) functorial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints: (ii) use filtration expression γ(M)=∑γ(A/p_i). (iii) show γ(A/p)=0 for nonzero prime p when A PID/local field and use rank morphism to Z. (i),(iv) left to reader or follow indicated exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: K1(A) and its relations to K(A) (Exercise 7.27)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let F1(A) = isomorphism classes of finitely generated flat A-modules. Construct K1(A) analogously and denote image γ1(M). (i) Tensor product induces a commutative ring structure on K1(A) with unit γ1(A). (ii) Tensor induces a K1(A)-module structure on K(A) with γ1(M)·γ(N)=γ(M⊗N). (iii) If A local Noetherian then K1(A) ≅ Z. (iv) Extension of scalars gives functorial ring homomorphism f!: K1(A)→K1(B). (v) Projection formula f!( f!(x)·y ) = x·f!(y) for finite f.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use properties of tensor product of finitely generated flat modules, previous exercises (e.g. Exercise 2.8i), and the argument given for (v) at the end of the exercise. Remark: for finite-dimensional regular rings, ε:K1(A)→K(A) is an isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artin rings characterization (Theorem 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: A ring A is Artin if and only if A is Noetherian and dim A = 0. Consequently, an Artin ring A is a finite-length A-module and results about chains of ideals apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Theorem 8.5 as given; apply Propositions 6.7 and 6.8 to chains in Artin rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization of Noetherian local Artin rings (Proposition 8.6 restatement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal m. Exactly one holds: (i) m^n ≠ m^{n+1} for all n and A is not Artin; or (ii) m^n = 0 for some n, in which case A is Artin local. In particular, A is Artin iff m is nilpotent. Also every proper ideal of an Artin local ring is m-primary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a restatement of Proposition 8.6 and is used in subsequent proofs such as Theorem 8.7.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure theorem for Artin rings (Theorem 8.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Artin ring A is uniquely (up to isomorphism) a finite direct product of Artin local rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness can be seen by analyzing minimal idempotents; kernels of maps to factors are maximal among proper ideals generated by an idempotent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization (*) in Artin local rings (Proposition 8.8 comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an Artin local ring (A,m) with property (*) 'there exists x∈m such that every ideal of A is of the form (x^r)', the proposition's proof shows that (*) is equivalent to listed conditions (i),(ii),(iii) in the book.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the structure of Artin local rings and the proof of Proposition 8.8 to verify equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic powers contained in primary components (Exercise 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given minimal primary decomposition 0 = ∩_{i=1}^n q_i with q_i p_i-primary in a Noetherian ring, for each i there exists integer r_i such that p_i^{(r_i)} ⊂ q_i. If q_i is isolated primary component then q_i = p_i^{(r)} for some r; if embedded the symbolic powers are all distinct and one can obtain infinitely many minimal decompositions differing only in the p_i-component.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Proposition 7.14 (every ideal contains a power of its radical) and properties of isolated vs embedded components; for isolated components use that A_{p_i} is Artin so powers stabilize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterizations of Artinian rings via Spec (Exercise 8.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian ring A the following are equivalent: (i) A is Artinian; (ii) Spec(A) is discrete and finite; (iii) Spec(A) is discrete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exercise 1.22, Theorem 8.5 (Artin ⇔ Noetherian + dim 0), and Theorem 8.7 (structure theorem) to derive equivalences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artinian finitely generated k-algebras are finite (Exercise 8.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let k be a field and A a finitely generated k-algebra. Then A is Artinian iff A is a finite k-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If A is Artinian, use Theorem 8.7 to reduce to Artin local rings and Nullstellensatz to show residue fields finite over k, then finite length ⇒ finite k-algebra. Conversely, finite k-algebra implies ideals are k-vector subspaces so satisfy DCC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relations between finite morphisms and fiber properties (Exercise 8.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite type map f: A→B consider: (i) f finite; (ii) fibers of f* are discrete subspaces; (iii) for each prime p of A, B⊗_A k(p) is a finite k(p)-algebra; (iv) fibers of f* are finite. Show (i)⇒(ii)⇔(iii)⇒(iv). Also ask: if f is integral and fibers finite, is f necessarily finite?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To show (i)⇒(iii) use localization and integrality lemmas (Lemma 85). For the last question, consider A,B fields and the example Z→Z[1/2] shows (ii) need not imply (i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite covering in Noether normalization context (Exercise 8.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the context of Noether Normalization, show that X is a finite covering of L (i.e., the number of points of X lying over a given point of L is finite and bounded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the arguments from the Noether Normalization Section referenced (Chapter 5 exercise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounded lengths of chains of primary ideals (Exercise 8.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Noetherian and q a p-primary ideal. Consider chains of p-primary ideals from q to p. Show all such chains are of finite bounded length and all maximal chains have same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to the local situation A_p and use that the poset of p-primary ideals between q and p corresponds to proper ideals of the Artin local quotient A_p / q_p; use Proposition 8.6 and facts about finite length Artin rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterizations of discrete valuation rings (Proposition 9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a Noetherian local domain A of dimension one with maximal ideal m and residue field k, the following are equivalent: (i) A is a discrete valuation ring; (ii) A is integrally closed; (iii) m is principal; (iv) dim_k(m/m^2)=1; (v) every non-zero ideal is a power of m; (vi) there exists x such that every non-zero ideal is (x^n). Variants (v') and (vi') assert uniqueness of such power decompositions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the equivalences and the statements in the proof (Statement (B) etc.) to derive the equivalences; see detailed proof in the book and comments in the text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof remarks for equivalences involving Artin quotients (Section 10.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: When proving (iv)⇒(v) in Proposition 9.2, justify that A/m^n is Artin (apply Proposition 8.6), and in other equivalences refer to Statement (B) used in the proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text flags specific references where the book's proof makes implicit claims; use Proposition 8.6 and earlier statements to fill gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of Dedekind domains (Exercise 9.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be Dedekind and S a multiplicative subset. Show S^{-1}A is either Dedekind or the field of fractions. If S ≠ A\\{0}, show extension of ideals induces a surjective homomorphism on ideal class groups H→H_S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section 6.1.6 for guidance on localizing Dedekind domains and class group behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gauss's lemma for content of polynomials (Exercise 9.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a Dedekind domain and f,g∈A[x] with content c(f)=(coefficients of f), prove c(fg)=c(f)c(g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Localize at every maximal ideal and reduce to the PID/local case; use Exercise 1.2iv and show inclusion of localized contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian valuation ring iff DVR (Exercise 9.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A valuation ring (other than a field) is Noetherian if and only if it is a discrete valuation ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valuation rings have totally ordered ideals, so finitely generated ideals are principal; hence a noetherian valuation ring is a PID; non-field PID of dim 1 gives DVR by Proposition 9.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local domain with principal maximal ideal and nil intersection implies DVR (Exercise 9.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A be a local domain not a field with maximal ideal m principal and ⋂_{n≥1} m^n = (0). Prove A is a DVR and define valuation w: A\{0}→N with properties w(ab)=w(a)+w(b), units characterized by w=0, and every nonzero ideal equals (p^{w(a)}) for appropriate generator p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take p generating m and define w(a) as minimal n with a∈p^n\p^{n+1}. Show multiplicativity and deduce principal ideal property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure theorem for finitely generated torsion modules over Dedekind domains (Exercise 9.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let M be a finitely generated torsion A-module over Dedekind domain A. Prove M ≅ ⊕_i A/p_i^{n_i} uniquely (finite direct sum of modules A/p^{n}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use annihilator factorization and decompose M as module over A/ann(M) which is a product of local Artin rings; reduce to the principal ideal domain case at each factor and use standard structure theorem for modules over PID/local principal rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Every ideal in A/a principal and 2-generator property (Exercise 9.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Let A Dedekind and 0≠a⊂A. Show every ideal in A/a is principal. Deduce every ideal in A can be generated by at most two elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to showing any nontrivial quotient of A is a principal ideal ring (use previous exercise), then given x∈a nonzero find y so that a=(x,y).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity and topology of completions (Completions comment 1, Section 11.1.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: When discussing completions (G^∧, H^∧) and induced maps, ensure topologies are defined via subgroups (G_n)^∧ viewed as subgroups of G^∧ so that canonical map c:G→G^∧ is continuous with dense image; if f:G→H is continuous then f^∧:G^∧→H^∧ is continuous. This assumes 0 has countable fundamental system of neighborhoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Corollary 10.4 and view completions appropriately; the text points out an omission in the book and provides the corrected viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notation remark about quotients G/G_n (Completions comment 2, Section 11.1.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The penultimate display should be read as G/G_n when considering successive quotients in the construction of completions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a minor notational remark clarifying the display in the book.
